answer: An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the river check immediately, the velvet audit keeps the resolved set and the nebula replay makes public exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 195 aliases hence pays the reading cost 195 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 20 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
